subject: Integration & Dedicated Capacity: implementation path and open questions
messages:
From: Anna Kwan <anna.kwan@finex-corp.com>
To: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call — next steps on integration and dedicated capacity

Thanks for the call this morning — that was helpful. A few follow-ups from our side so we can internalize and move toward a procurement decision:

1) Integration mechanics: we need a one-page summary of SDK bootstrap/auth steps (service account vs API key, mTLS option), routing for dev/prod, and how structured output/tool-calls are surfaced to our backend.

2) Embeddings & rerankers: high-level guidance on embedding size, approximate cost per 1M embeddings, and options for reranker: hosted vs bring-your-own.

3) Dedicated sizing: we sketched numbers on the call but Procurement would like a recommended committed capacity for 3 months (concurrency targets, tokens/sec, queue sizing) to include in the contract.

Can you send a short implementation path and an updated mutual action plan? Also looping in Procurement (procurement@finex-corp.com) — they may have specific PO timelines.

Thanks,
Anna
Sr. Engineering Manager, Finex Corp

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kwan <anna.kwan@finex-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call — next steps on integration and dedicated capacity

Anna — great to meet earlier. Attached is a concise implementation path and a draft mutual-action-plan (attached as mutual-action-plan.md). High-level answers below; I'll follow with a technical appendix for your infra team Monday.

Quick answers:
- SDK bootstrap & auth: we support API keys and customer-managed service accounts. For Dedicated we recommend a service-account + short-lived tokens via your KMS; mTLS is available for Private deployments if required. SDK install is a 2-line pip/npm + environment variable for credentials.

- Routing and environments: create two logical routes (dev/prod) in Redwood Console. Route policies allow pinning model variants and fallback chains (e.g., cost-fallback to a quantized variant). We can wire dev routes into your staging cluster before cutover.

- Structured output / tool-calls: the SDK supports function/tool calling (JSON schema + routing). Tool calls are returned in a structured payload; your backend consumes the tool call and responds with tool outputs which Redwood can re-inject into the model context. We'll include a sample payload in the appendix.

- Embeddings & rerankers: recommended embedding dim 1536 for semantic search; approximate hosted cost ~ $60 per 1M embed units (estimate — will confirm). Reranking can run as a lightweight hosted post-rank step or in your VPC for data-sensitive workflows.

- Dedicated sizing (recommended commit for 3 months): start with 8x A100-equivalent concurrency slots (targets: 75 qps conversational, 250 ms median token latency for short prompts), with an auto-scale buffer to 12 for burst. Queue depth: 200 requests (FIFO with priority routing). We'll provide a capacity spreadsheet for fine-tuning (attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll upload the detailed appendix + sizing workbook by Monday.
2) Schedule a 45-min tech sync (infra + security) — can we target Tue 11/24?
3) Procurement: Marissa, can you share contract timeline and any template terms we should be aware of?

Thanks — sending the attachments now.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Cell: (555) 483-2171

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.md (stub), redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (stub)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call — follow-ups (autoscale, queues, auth)

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 12:45 PM nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Dedicated sizing (recommended commit for 3 months): start with 8x A100-equivalent concurrency slots ... Queue depth: 200 requests (FIFO with priority routing).

Team — a couple of technical clarifications I want to pull together before the tech sync with Finex: 

1) Autoscale policy: do we recommend time-based scaling + utilization thresholds (token/sec) or only request-queue-depth thresholds? Proposed: primary autoscale on sustained token throughput (5-min moving avg) and secondary on queue depth > 150 for 2 consecutive mins.

2) Concurrency limit semantics: We need to call out per-connection vs per-account concurrency. Finex expects per-route concurrency (separate dev/prod). Our Dedicated offering enforces per-tenant concurrency caps at the Router layer — confirm how burst is handled (token-bucket vs queue). Sean — can you add a short blurb on how the router currently handles bursts and KV-cache warmups?

3) Embedding throughput: if they do large batch embed uploads (50k/day), recommend batching window and suggestions for backpressure handling (we should provide sample client code).

4) Security: Anna asked about SOC2 evidence; we should package the SOC2 checklist and note the option for customer-managed keys. Mina suggested an evidence bundle — Dev, can you make sure SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf is the one we give them?

I’ll take ownership of the tech-sync agenda — we should block 30–40 mins and reserve time for procurement Qs.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Anna Kwan <anna.kwan@finex-corp.com>, procurement <procurement@finex-corp.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call — confirmed plan and Tue tech sync

Anna / Procurement — thanks again. Recap and confirmed items before Tue 11/24 11:00 PT tech sync (calendar invite sent):

Decisions / proposals:
- Auth: Dedicated -> service-account short-lived tokens (we will ship an example token broker; Finex to confirm KMS decision). mTLS not required for Dedicated but available for Private.
- SDK: quickstart will be a 2-line install + env var; sample code for structured tool-calls included in appendix.
- Routing: two routes (finex-staging, finex-prod) with independent concurrency caps in the Router.
- Autoscale: primary trigger = 5-min avg token/sec > threshold; secondary = queue depth > 150 for 2+ mins. Initial scaling policy: target 70% slot utilization before scale-up.
- Sizing: initial commit = 8 concurrency slots (A100-equivalent), burst to 12; queue depth 200; expected baseline of 75 qps conversational. See attached redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx for the workbook with sensitivity analysis.
- Embeddings: recommend 1536-dim; rough hosted estimate $60 / 1M embeddings (ballpark). Reranker options documented (hosted post-rank vs run-in-vpc).

Attachments provided: mutual-action-plan.md, redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf.

Action items before the sync:
1) Finex: confirm KMS preference and whether Procurement needs a draft SOW by EOD Wed.
2) Redwood (Marissa): draft procurement timeline and any required contract exceptions.
3) Redwood (Sean/Dev): prepare a 10-min tech appendix (router burst behavior, KV-cache warmup guidance, sample embed-batch client code).

If Procurement wants a separate legal/finance touchpoint before the sync, we can accommodate. Looking forward to the call — we’ll aim to produce a 1-page tech appendix during the meeting for immediate use in Procurement conversations.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.md, SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf
